Let’s work through it.

Start with the simplest checks. Test one change at a time.

Troubleshooting · 6 MIN READ

Wi-Fi connected. Internet missing?

First check whether the problem affects one device or every device. That tells you whether to start with your computer or your network. Try the steps below in order and test after each one.

Read the guide ↗Troubleshooting · 7 MIN READ

Why is my computer running slowly?

A slow computer may be short of memory or storage space, busy with background work, or getting too hot. Start by finding what is busy instead of installing a cleaner app.

Read the guide ↗Troubleshooting · 5 MIN READ

Bluetooth won’t connect? Start here.

Charge the accessory, put it into pairing mode, and check whether it is already connected to another device. Bluetooth being switched on is not the same as being discoverable.

Read the guide ↗Troubleshooting · 5 MIN READ

What to do when a computer won’t start

Separate a power problem from a display or startup problem. Check for indicator lights, fan noise, and anything on the screen before deciding what to try.

Read the guide ↗Troubleshooting · 3 MIN READ

iPhone or iPad won’t connect to Wi-Fi

Check Settings → Wi-Fi first. A checkmark beside a network means you joined it, but does not guarantee internet access. Compare with another device on the same network.

Read the guide ↗Troubleshooting · 3 MIN READ

Google Nest speaker won’t connect to Wi-Fi

Check power, network credentials, and distance from the router before changing router settings. These checks apply to Google Nest and Home speakers and displays, not every smart-home product.
